title: Which open hydraulic circuit gets a small excavator closest to stock energy use for the least money?
lede: research programme: which buildable hydraulic circuit gets a small excavator closest to stock energy use; on a measured 6 t load-sensing wheel loader (Zenodo, CC BY) the measured LS margin is 24.9 bar, the model's LS rung matches measured pump energy to 2.3%, and an open-centre pump on the same motion needs at least 1.37 times the energy for any bypass law (1.54 times and 14.7% more fuel at a 10 bar spool drop, with the motion threshold measured from the data); earlier milestones are model sweeps with sourced margins and valve curves
summary: An open research programme on which hydraulic circuit a small shop can build from catalogue parts to get a 1.5 to 3 t excavator closest to stock energy use, and at what parts cost. Milestone 1 is a stdlib model of pump-shaft energy for three circuits (fixed-displacement open-centre, load-sensing, ideal independent metering; analytic single-actuator check, 6 tests) and a 2,916-case grid on one four-phase cycle: load-sensing uses a median 47% of open-centre shaft energy (22 to 81%), saving more as flow demand falls (31%, 47%, 63% of open-centre at 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 of full flow), and metering uses a median 80% of load-sensing, 88% with equal actuator pressures and 74% at 1.5 times the reference spread. The ordering holds in every case but only because each rung removes a loss term, so it is a code check rather than a finding. The cycle, pressures, flows and margins are illustrative values written from memory and swept, not sourced; there are no dynamics, leakage, line losses, energy recovery or parts costs; the DOI registry was unreachable so references were checked by web search, not cite_check. Milestone 2a repeats the comparison on 20,000 random cycles inside a machine envelope (pump 45 L/min, 20 to 180 bar, taken from an unopened search summary of one mini-excavator listing): load-sensing uses a median 44% of open-centre energy, metering 72% of load-sensing (87% at equal actuator pressures), and H3 fails per case in about a third of equal-pressure cycles. The cycles are random, not measured. Preliminary; arithmetic only, nothing run on a machine. Milestone 5n (2026-11-11) adds the first measured machine: a public 440 s trace of a 6 t load-sensing wheel loader loading gravel (Linjama et al., Zenodo 10639199, CC BY 4.0) with pump and cylinder pressures, flows and ECU fuel rate. The measured load-sensing margin is a median 24.9 bar (standby 30.8 bar); the model's constant-margin load-sensing rung reproduces measured pump hydraulic energy to 2.3% (per-cycle 95% bootstrap 1.3 to 3.4%); actuators receive 73% of pump hydraulic energy. A counterfactual open-centre pump on the same motion would use 1.46 times the hydraulic energy (sweep 1.24 to 1.79) and add 12.3% to machine fuel (6.2 to 21.7%), refuting two of four registered predictions; the figure depends most on a small-flow threshold for the open-centre bypass chosen after a first, buggy run. A wheel loader, not an excavator; valve drops swept, not sourced. Milestone 5o measures that threshold instead: the flow noise floor in windows where the piston does not move is 0.80 L/min (lift) and 1.76 L/min (tilt); with it, open-centre needs 1.54 times the load-sensing pump hydraulic energy (per-cycle 95% bootstrap 1.46 to 1.63) and adds 14.7% fuel at a 10 bar spool drop, and a floor valid for any bypass closing law (spool drop 0) is 1.37 to 1.43 times. A motion rule from piston position alone gives 1.51. All four registered predictions held. With the least drop any Danfoss PVG 32 spool can have fully open (milestone 5r), the ratio is 1.42 (11.3% more fuel): on this machine the open-centre penalty comes from the fixed pump, not the spool. The lift flow exceeds the largest PVG 32 spool's rating in 11% of moving samples, where that floor is extrapolated. Milestone 5t evaluates the closed-form break-even margin on this record: load-sensing would match the best open-centre counterfactual only at an 87 bar margin (per Y-cycle 59 to 143 bar, median 81), against 20 to 30 bar on the synthetic excavator cycles, so the measured 24.9 bar margin leaves large headroom; about 90% of it is surplus flow from a fixed pump whose mean flow is 1.78 times the mean demand. The counterfactual keeps the loader's own pump size.
